criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Slide 1 is close to a 10. Nineteen mirror wafers in a quartz boat on black epoxy, with the row and rods running off the right edge, a lit rim, contact shadow and a median L* of 5.3 (art_preflight). Slides 3, 4 and 5 hold the same bench and flood with good contact and dark fields. The slide 6 relief tray reads its 12 / 4 and a half / 19 counts at feed size. Three frames hold the score down. Slide 8 has a low-poly, lumpy kit-person head filling the lower left, and its subject is a laptop beside a black fin stack that reads as a heat sink. On slide 7 the copper half grown layer covers about a sixth of the frame on generic diagonal terraces and reads as a scrap at 432 px. On slide 2 the 'Lubbock County' label sits outside the raised square, in the footer row, which breaks the storyboard's own acceptance line. Slide 9's relief has cast_fraction 0.136, the lowest in the deck, and reads more as a UI panel than a lit object.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: The wafer boat at one pitch is a real changing motif: nineteen and open (1), twelve capped (3), twelve beside twelve (4), four and a half (5), all three in one tray (6), back on a desk (8). One cold flood comes from the left and value stays dark throughout, with no strobe. The three plan-view reliefs (2, 7, 9) leave the bench world. Slide 7 especially looks like it came from another deck. Dusk_gold holds its single meaning (November) on 1, 6 and 9.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces: $19 (c1, nov_floor_m), $12 (c15), $24 (c16), $4.5 (c17), 2023 (c19), November 13th (c2), $1 million per wafer (drawing unit). The careful handling of 'over' and 'roughly' is good, and so is printing no total. The deck then invents a third kind of number. Slide 6 says 'January was $12 million exactly' and labels the row 'January, exact'. c15's quote is only 'a $12 million Texas Semiconductor Innovation Fund (TSIF) grant award'. Nothing in the claims says the figure is exact rather than rounded. Smaller faults: the slide 2 label 'Lubbock County' and the caption's #LubbockCounty name a county no claim names. 'Not built yet' is the fact-checker's inference from 'will help establish'. All three sources are Texas Tech's own news releases, and the first comment calls them 'three official records', which oversells press releases.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: What happened, where, who pays and what is missing are all clear. Nothing tells a Texan what they can do. The close is a question, not a next step. The stake for Lubbock or the South Plains is never stated.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover earns the swipe. Frames 3 to 6 build the counting argument well, and 9's empty IN SERVICE recess lands the close. Frame 2 delays the payoff. Frame 7 interrupts the run from 6 to 8.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean and on register and obeys the house rules. 'Lubbock has a computing cluster on paper.' is a good line. 'Drawn to illustrate' repeats on seven of nine frames. Slide 7's dek is close to verbatim release language. No South Plains specificity beyond the city name.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: Topic is clear of the 30-day window. The floodlit interior diverges from nos. 74 to 76. Two familiar moves: counting units as a drawing scale, and a lab bench close to no. 65's foundry. Slide 8's laptop-on-desk shot is a stock kit shot.

hard_fails: Unverified fact presented as verified: slide 6 body 'January was $12 million exactly' and label 'January, exact', cited to c15, whose quote says only 'a $12 million ... grant award'. No claim establishes that the figure is exact rather than rounded. Repair: drop 'exactly' and 'exact', or add a claim that verifies exactness.
one_sentence_fix: Strip 'exactly' and 'January, exact' from slide 6 and rebuild the three-kinds-of-number argument on what the sources actually say, then give slide 8 the nineteen-wafer boat as its true subject in place of the laptop and low-poly head.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A low-poly kit-person head over the left third and a black fin stack that reads as a heat sink. The nineteen-wafer boat is unreadable as wafers.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Cut the person. Drop the camera to bench height over the desk edge so the quartz boat of nineteen mirror wafers fills the lower half, lit by the flood with the warm strip behind. Keep the laptop small at the back as the scale reference.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The copper half-grown layer covers about a sixth of the frame on uniform diagonal terraces and reads as a scrap at 432 px.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Show the terraces as lit risers across the full width and several separate copper islands on the top terrace, filling at least a third of the frame, under the same left flood.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The 'Lubbock County' label sits outside the raised square in the footer row.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Move the label inside the raised county face, centred, and raise the relief height so the county's lit north edge and its cast carry the frame.
